title: Squash Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Squash Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Squash nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, potassium and magnesium in kalabasa, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Squash nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your kalabasa (squash) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, magnesium, phosphorus, calcium, boron and zinc. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Young squash fruit with a black, rotted blossom end from calcium shortage
heroImage.credit: Mary Ann Hansen, Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University, CC BY 3.0 US, via ipmimages.org

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, magnesium and phosphorus move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But calcium, boron and zinc stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which squash nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a squash nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest squash nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in squash

Older leaves turn pale, yellowing starts at the leaf tips and spreads up the vine, and old leaves die or drop. Vines are stunted and fruits are small, pale and thick. You see it most at this stage: rapid vine growth and fruit set.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in kalabasa
Sandy soils, heavy rain, low organic matter, and no side dressing before fruiting.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage leaves green veins on the old leaves. Downy mildew gives angular yellow patches. To be sure, old leaves yellow first. Soil test and leaf tissue test.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate at the soil test rate, in one or two doses before the fruits form. Give a urea leaf spray at 10 grams per liter of water (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) every 15 days for pumpkin (Cucurbita moschata, the same kind as Philippine kalabasa). Side dress 5 to 10 grams of Urea 46 0 0 a plant, about 1 to 2 bags per hectare, every two to three weeks from flowering, and water it in.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea (46 0 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Crown Champion Ammonium Sulfate** by Aqua Hydroponic Prime Ventures (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur), **Agripower 46 0 0 (Locally Blended) Coated** by Green Acres Agri Tech and **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, add manure in the hills before planting and side dress before fruit set.
Potassium deficiency in squash

Older leaves yellow and scorch, cup or curl upward, and get dead spots along the midrib. Shoots die back, stems weaken, fewer female flowers form and fruit quality drops. You see it most at this stage: flowering and fruit filling.
Why potassium deficiency happens in kalabasa
Sandy or acid soils, heavy rain, and no potash after planting.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage yellows between veins first. Potassium burns the edges first. To be sure, soil test for potassium and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For immediate relief, give a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) with a sticker. Keep pH above 6 with lime or dolomite. A usual dose is 1 to 2 bags of Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Sulfate of potash 0 0 50 per hectare, split from flowering to fruit fill.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash (MOP)** by Atlas Fertilizer (0 0 60), **Simplot Sulfate 0 0 50** by Nutranta, **Potassium Nitrate** by Parafield (13 0 46) and **Qrop Mix Production 14 0 23 plus 13 Cao** by Farmtech Agriland (14 0 23 with 9.3 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash at planting and at flowering. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.
Magnesium deficiency in squash

Yellowing between the veins starts on the oldest leaves and moves up the vine. The leaf centre yellows while the edges stay green. The yellow tissue can turn red or brown, die and drop out, leaving holes. Leaves fall early and yield drops. You see it most at this stage: fruit enlargement.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in kalabasa
Sandy soils, low pH, dry years, and heavy potash, lime or ammonium fertilizer.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage yellows the whole leaf. Manganese toxicity on very acid soil gives bronze spots. To be sure, soil test for magnesium, potassium and pH.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

Try magnesium sulfate in a band near the plants at about 80 kg per hectare. Keep the pH near 6.5. Leaf sprays seldom cure a serious shortage. Do not apply magnesium with potash. For quick help, spray Magnesium sulfate at 1 to 2 percent (160 to 320 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) two or three times, 10 to 14 days apart.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Agsmart Kieserite Granule** (20 percent sulfur and 16.3 percent magnesium), **DDDD Planter's Choice Magnesium Sulphate Monohydrate** by Modern Time (15.1 percent magnesium) and **Zetryl MAG 9** by Zetryl Chem (9 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomite on acid soils before planting. Test the soil every two or three years.
Phosphorus deficiency in squash
Leaves and veins turn purplish, shoots are short and thin, leaves look dull and shrivelled, and yield is poor. You see it most at this stage: early vine growth.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in kalabasa
Acid or iron rich soils, low organic matter, and no phosphorus at planting.
How to tell it apart
Root knot nematodes also stunt vines. Look for root galls. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply phosphorus in the hill based on the soil test. Use single superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate or bone meal for the long term. Uptake is best near pH 6.2 to 7.0. A usual basal dose is 4 to 6 bags of Complete 14 14 14 per hectare, 10 to 20 grams a hill, mixed into the soil at transplanting.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Philphos 18 46 0 (Di Ammonium Phosphate)**, **Atlas Super Gro (16 20 0)** by Atlas Fertilizer, **Amigo Planters Granular Single Super Phosphate** by La Filipina (0 18 0 with 11 percent sulfur) and **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals (0 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use complete fertilizer or 16 20 0 in the hill at planting.
Calcium deficiency in squash

blocks.alt: Young squash fruit with a black, rotted blossom end from calcium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Mary Ann Hansen, Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University, CC BY 3.0 US, via ipmimages.org

blocks.text: Fruits develop a sunken, leathery rot at the blossom end, starting as small light brown spots on young fruit. Young leaves show yellow stripes along the midrib, crinkle and scorch at the edges and become brittle. Vine tips can die back. Fruits may be small or tasteless. You see it most at this stage: early fruit growth, in hot dry spells.
Why calcium deficiency happens in kalabasa
Too little calcium reaching the fruit because of uneven or poor watering, dry or salty soil, sandy soils and heavy ammonium fertilizer. Excess phosphorus and low boron add to it.
How to tell it apart

Poor pollination makes young fruit shrivel and yellow from the tip without the leathery patch. Fruit rots from fungi are soft and mouldy from the start. To be sure, soil test for calcium and pH, and a check of your watering.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

Water evenly and mulch. On acid soil, try lime at about 250 kg per hectare when pH is 5.5 to 6, or about 840 kg per hectare in two doses when pH is 3.5 to 4.5. Gypsum on soil that is not acid. Remove rotten fruits. Lime 2 to 4 weeks before planting. Calcium sprays go on young fruit from fruit set.

Sold here with calcium: **Micronized Activated Calcite** by CMCS Agricultural Products (37.6 percent calcium), **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **Titon Pro** by Vast Agro (27.2 percent calcium, 6.1 percent silicon and 3.6 percent magnesium) and **Calcipro** by Ramgo (15.5 0 0 with 18.8 percent calcium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soil before planting, keep watering steady and avoid heavy ammonium fertilizer. Test the soil every two or three years. Keep potash in balance with magnesium and calcium.
Boron deficiency in squash
New leaves are malformed and the plant grows bushy as buds die. Young fruits drop, and fruits show corky marks, streaks and cracks. You see it most at this stage: flowering and fruit set.
Why boron deficiency happens in kalabasa
Sandy soils, overlimed soils, low organic matter and drought.
How to tell it apart
Poor pollination also drops young fruits but leaves stay normal. To be sure, soil test for boron and a leaf tissue test. In a soil test, less than 0.5 ppm of boron is low.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Try borax in the soil at about 10 kg per hectare or a borax spray at 1 gram per liter of water (16 grams in a 16 liter sprayer). Squash has a medium boron need, about 2.2 kg of boron per hectare before planting. Do not mix borax with calcium or ammonium fertilizers.

Sold here with boron: **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl Chem (11 percent boron), **Fertibagra 15G** by Unilox Far East Resources (14.6 percent boron), **B17 (Boric Acid)** by Newman Chemicals (17 percent boron) and **Better Yield** by Bacphil Planters Fertilizer (0 0 0.9 with 10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add a small boron dose to the basal fertilizer on sandy soils. Test the soil every two or three years. Keep organic matter up with compost, manure or crop residues.
Zinc deficiency in squash

Young leaves yellow between the veins and can turn white. Leaves are pale with green veins, the spaces between leaves are short and leaves form distorted rosettes. You see it most at this stage: vine growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in kalabasa
High pH or overlimed soils, heavy phosphorus and waterlogged soils.
How to tell it apart
Mosaic viruses also give small, mottled leaves, often with aphids around. To be sure, soil test for zinc and pH, and a leaf tissue test. In a soil test, less than 0.8 ppm of zinc is low.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Try zinc sulfate in the soil at about 20 kg per hectare. In severe cases a morning spray of zinc sulfate at 2 grams plus calcium carbonate at 2.5 grams per liter of water (40 grams in a 16 liter sprayer). Do not apply zinc and phosphate together. Give the soil dose at planting or when the rains begin, and sprays on young growth.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester (22 percent zinc), **Tierramino ZN** by Unilox Far East Resources (7 0 0 with 10 percent zinc), **Semia** by SCL Filipinas (20 percent zinc) and **Omex Zynergy** by Jardine Distribution (3.8 percent zinc and 2.1 percent copper). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep soil pH between 5 and 7.5. Test the soil every two or three years.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any squash nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your kalabasa needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Squash nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my kalabasa leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: older leaves yellow from the tips and drop, and fruits are small and pale. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in squash?
items.a: Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate at the soil test rate, in one or two doses before the fruits form. Give a urea leaf spray at 10 grams per liter of water (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) every 15 days for pumpkin (Cucurbita moschata, the same kind as Philippine kalabasa).

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in squash?
items.a: Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses. For immediate relief, give a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water (160 grams in a 16 liter sprayer) with a sticker.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes magnesium deficiency in squash?
items.a: Try magnesium sulfate in a band near the plants at about 80 kg per hectare. Keep the pH near 6.5.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my kalabasa lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the squash nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
